info.title: Internet Weather API
info.description:
Internet Weather observes the public internet, detects meaningful change in the
AI-engineering ecosystem, and explains it with traceable evidence.

The frontend consumes only this API. Provider APIs are never exposed directly.

Every data response carries a `freshness` object stating when the signals were
computed and how many days of observation support them. Findings carry an
`epistemic_status` of `observation`, `inference`, `hypothesis` or `unknown`, so
speculation is never presented as fact.

get.description:
Always 200.

A degraded API is still a working API: contracts and vocabulary resolve
without a database. Returning 500 here would make an ordinary cold start
look like an outage.

get.summary: The Trends page, in one call
get.description:
Bounded by design: four ranked bands plus recent events.

A single request so the page paints at once — assembling one screen from four
round trips is what makes an interface feel like a dashboard.

ChatReply.title: ChatReply
ChatReply.description: A Copilot answer. Grounded in Internet Weather data or it does not ship.

as_of.title: As Of
as_of.description: ISO date of the latest computed signal day.

observed_days.title: Observed Days
observed_days.description: Distinct days of observation backing these signals.

degraded_reason.title: Degraded Reason
degraded_reason.description: Why data is missing, when it is. Null when has_data is true.

DataFreshness.title: DataFreshness
DataFreshness.description:
How current, and how trustworthy, the numbers behind a response are.

Present on every data response. A platform that claims to observe the
internet has to be explicit about when it last actually looked.

EpistemicStatus.title: EpistemicStatus
EpistemicStatus.description:
Required label on every generated claim.

Enforced at the contract level so speculation can never be presented as
fact. See CLAUDE.md, "LLM Philosophy".

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: The measured value that triggered this, when applicable.

EvidenceLink.title: EvidenceLink
EvidenceLink.description:
A traceable source for a claim.

Present on every event so "show me the evidence" is answerable without a
round trip through the research engine.

Finding.title: Finding
Finding.description:
One claim, with its epistemic standing attached.

``epistemic_status`` is required, not optional. That is the mechanism by
which speculation cannot be presented as fact.

Health.title: Health
Health.description:
Liveness plus honest degradation.

``status`` is ``ok`` when data can be served and ``degraded`` when the API is
up but has no database. Degraded is a real product state, not a failure: the
contracts and vocabulary still resolve.

IngestionSummary.title: IngestionSummary
IngestionSummary.description: Last run per job. How you know whether the observatory is actually looking.

RelationshipType.title: RelationshipType
RelationshipType.description: Edges between technologies, used by Explore and the Research page.

RepoRelation.title: RepoRelation
RepoRelation.description: How a repository relates to the technology it sensors.

RepositorySensor.title: RepositorySensor
RepositorySensor.description: A repository observed on behalf of a technology.

question.title: Question
question.description: Optional focus, e.g. 'Why is MCP accelerating?'

unknowns.title: Unknowns
unknowns.description: What the evidence could not settle.

star_velocity_7d.title: Star Velocity 7D
star_velocity_7d.description: Weighted stars/day over the trailing 7 days.

star_acceleration.title: Star Acceleration
star_acceleration.description: Change in velocity — what 'heating up' actually means.

anomaly_z.title: Anomaly Z
anomaly_z.description: Standard deviations from this technology's own baseline.

sample_days.title: Sample Days
sample_days.description: Observed days backing this row. Low values mean low confidence.

SignalSnapshot.title: SignalSnapshot
SignalSnapshot.description:
The measured numbers behind a weather state.

Every field here is an OBSERVATION or a deterministic transform of one. The
UI may show these without an epistemic caveat.

Subdomain.title: Subdomain
Subdomain.description: Technology subdomains within the AI-engineering domain.

SubdomainClimate.title: SubdomainClimate
SubdomainClimate.description: Aggregate weather for one subdomain — the radar's regional readout.

TechnologyCard.title: TechnologyCard
TechnologyCard.description:
One technology as it appears on Trends, including its hover preview.

Deliberately self-sufficient: the hover intelligence preview must not fire a
second request, so the sparkline and explanation ship with the card.

TechnologyDetail.title: TechnologyDetail
TechnologyDetail.description: The Research page header: what we know, and what it rests on.

Vocabulary.title: Vocabulary
Vocabulary.description: Everything the UI needs to label data it did not compute.

WeatherState.title: WeatherState
WeatherState.description:
Computed atmospheric state of a technology.

NEVER assign these by hand. They are the output of
``internetweather.analysis.weather_state.classify`` operating on measured
signals. A technology with insufficient history is STABLE with low
confidence — not EMERGING.

WeatherStateInfo.title: WeatherStateInfo
WeatherStateInfo.description:
Presentation metadata for one weather state.

Served so the frontend renders the semantic vocabulary from the API instead
of hardcoding glyphs that could drift from the classifier.
